_comment: #1278: how often CollaboratorPick.photoToPromote would actually fire.
It fires whenever ANY later photograph carries a stronger account than the
first. The broad trigger was deliberate (#983): a 'much stronger'
threshold would be a second constant calibrated against a population
nobody had measured. The cost of that choice is noise, and since #964 the
collaborator panel renders on every posting day, so a suggestion that
appeared on most posts would sit above the findings that need judgement
and teach everybody to skip the panel.
Taken by PhotoPromotionRateMeasurement against a COPY of the live store.
Counts only: no handles and no event names ever reach this file or the
terminal, because a tool reading a live system otherwise delivers real
names into transcripts by a route no repository scanner sees.
_reading: It fired on NONE of the six days where it could fire at all.
The 35 and the 6 are the numbers that matter together. Reporting 0 of 35
would read as a narrow trigger when most of those days simply carry no
tagged photograph with figures, and that is not a finding about the
trigger (L98). Reporting 0 of 6 alone would hide how little of the week
the suggestion can reach at all.
So: no evidence of noise, and no narrowing. Said plainly, six days is a
small sample and this is not proof it will never be noisy. What it is, is
a reading that can be taken again as the book fills, which is what #1278
asked for and what nothing could do before.
